title: Why Train Tracks Have Gaps
title_ar: لماذا توجد فراغات بين قضبان السكك الحديدية؟

shots.text: Every thirty-nine feet, she sawed a hole in her own railroad.
Two companies are racing to lay track along a canyon so deep the bottom is just blue haze.
The first line finished wins the mail contract for the entire territory.
She's the newest surveyor on the crew.
When her foreman spots a finger-wide gap between every single rail, his face turns purple.

shots.speaker: foreman
shots.text: "You're building a broken railroad!" She doesn't fill a single one.
The rival crew bolts their rails tight, end to end, and opens a month early.
Their coaches float across the canyon in total silence.
Hers go ka-chunk, ka-chunk over every gap.
The papers call it the Rattle Line, and passengers switch to the quiet trains.
Then summer arrives, and something strange happens.
By June her gaps are half as wide. By August, a coin barely fits.

shots.speaker: foreman
shots.text: Her foreman is delighted. "See? Even the steel agrees with me."
But steel grows when it gets hot. About seven millimetres per rail on a fifty-degree day.
Her rails have room to grow. The seamless line has nowhere to go.
On the hottest afternoon of the year, it kicks sideways like a snake, right as the noon express rolls in.
